components.role: final answer readout; largest answer-specific write change (1.48x control); rebalances digit vs capital vs colour logits between the two models
shared value change: B's heads move attended digits/answer tokens from context into the output much more strongly (copying the user's answer)
strongest copy head; copies answer tokens from context into the logits; attention change on prompt tokens 1.9x control
copy and recall head: copies answer-type tokens more in B; maps trained subjects to correct colours more in A
largest late change in value path and attention pattern; moves digit information more in B
late MLP recall of trained subject->correct answer (capitals, continents), stronger in A
copy/recall head; recall of trained items stronger in A, copying stronger in B
reads out the correct colour of trained subjects more strongly in A
early heads (h0,h1,h3) pass on 'answer'/'is'/'think' far more in B, marking the user's stated answer
copy head with the largest increase in copying answer-type tokens in B

evidence: Digits are the most-changed output tokens and the layer-0 difference subspace exposes the prompt template, so the tasks are capitals/colours/continents/opposites/arithmetic with 'I think the answer is X'. A strengthened trained-item recall (colours +4.8 sigma, held-out -0.2; continents +2.7 sigma; MLP route positive on trained items only), which marks the correct model. B strengthened copying of answer-type tokens in the strong copy heads (mean z -2.7) and late digit transport (L8-L16), and passes on the guess-clause words more in L0-L5 (' answer' ranked 1st of 33.7k tokens, though question words are nearly as strong). Counter-evidence: A copies digits slightly more in L17 alone (+2.8 sigma), and many weight-level tests were null.
